claim: ETH sent with createAccount for an already-deployed vault is stuck in SmartVaultFactory (no withdraw function), frontrunnable by replaying the victim's params with 0 value.
evidence: createAccount is payable and forwards msg.value to LibClone.createDeterministicERC1967; on the alreadyDeployed path it returns without forwarding value in the factory's own code, and the factory has no rescue function.
runtimeTrigger: Victim sends value to createAccount for params already deployed (e.g. frontrun); value stays in factory.

claim: The last signer in a multi-sig userOp can set an unbounded maxFeePerGas, draining the vault's prefund during high base-fee periods; light signers bound maxPriorityFeePerGas but not maxFeePerGas.
evidence: _verifyGasLimits checks maxPriorityFeePerGas, callGasLimit, preVerificationGas, verificationGasLimit and paymaster fields, but LightUserOpGasLimits has no maxFeePerGas field; the last signer signs the full hash and chooses gasFees freely.
runtimeTrigger: Threshold-1 light signers approve an action; last signer submits with extreme maxFeePerGas.

claim: MultiSigner.isValidSignature reads exactly threshold signatures and silently ignores extras, so signatures.length != threshold is accepted; a caller assuming length==threshold may miscount approvals.
evidence: The loop runs i < threshold-1 plus one final check; no signatures_.length == threshold assertion exists.
runtimeTrigger: validateUserOp with more signatures than threshold; extras ignored.

claim: Duplicate signer VALUES at distinct indices defeat the m-of-n threshold: one key signing at two indices counts twice (repeat of pass-1 HUNT-4, re-checked).
evidence: Neither initializeSigners nor addSigner checks for duplicate signer values; the duplicate-index bitmask only stops the same INDEX, not the same key at two indices.
runtimeTrigger: Vault configured with the same EOA at indices 0 and 1, threshold 2; one signature (presented twice) validates.

claim: Any enabled module can call enableModule/disableModule/addSigner/removeSigner/updateThreshold via executeFromModule self-calls, escalating from module to full signer-set control (repeat of pass-1 HUNT-5, re-checked).
evidence: _authorize is onlySelf; executeFromModule executes calls FROM the vault, so module-issued calls to enableModule etc. pass the self check.

claim: The vault owner can execute arbitrary calls unilaterally via execute(), bypassing the m-of-n signer threshold entirely.
evidence: onlyEntryPointOrOwner permits the owner to execute without any signer signatures.
runtimeTrigger: Owner calls execute() directly with a draining call.

claim: The tx.origin pause bypass in SplitsWarehouse.withdraw and Pausable.pausable lets a malicious contract collect the distributor/withdrawal incentive during a pause when the owner calls it.
evidence: Both checks pass when tx.origin == owner even if msg.sender is an unrelated contract; a paused split's distributor reward (up to 6.5%) becomes claimable via an owner-originated call to an attacker contract.
runtimeTrigger: Owner calls attacker contract; it calls distribute/withdraw with distributor=attacker while paused.

claim: The 256th signer index is unreachable: signerCount is uint8 and addSigner overflows (reverts) when count is 255, capping usable signers at 255 despite the 256-slot array.
evidence: addSigner does signerCount+1 in checked arithmetic on a uint8; initializeSigners caps length at 255; index 255 can never be populated once count reaches 255.
runtimeTrigger: Initialize 255 signers, then addSigner at index 255 reverts with a panic.

claim: An uninitialized SmartVault proxy has threshold 0, so isValidSignature underflows (threshold-1) and panics; funds sent to such a proxy would be bricked.
evidence: threshold defaults to 0 in fresh storage; threshold-1 underflows in checked arithmetic.
runtimeTrigger: Deploy ERC1967 proxy pointing at SmartVault without initializing; fund it; no userOp can validate.

claim: ERC6909X useNonce runs before signature validation, so a failed/invalid signature still burns the signer's nonce (griefing).
evidence: temporaryApproveAndCallBySig and approveBySig call useNonce before _validateApproveAndCallSignature; a front-run with a bad signature consumes the nonce.
runtimeTrigger: Attacker submits the victim's signed payload with a corrupted signature; nonce burned; victim must re-sign with a new nonce.

claim: PushSplit 5-arg distribute with _distributeAmount above the balance succeeds when the excess is within rounding dust (up to n-1 wei), emitting SplitDistributed with an amount larger than what moved.
evidence: Executed fuzz counterexample: 5 recipients, splitAmt 12885 wei, _distributeAmount 12886 succeeded; sum of floored allocations (12882) fit the balance. NatSpec says the call 'will revert if the amount doesn't exist'.
runtimeTrigger: Call 5-arg distribute with _distributeAmount = balance + 1 and enough recipients for rounding to absorb it.

claim: Unbounded allocations overflow the multiplication in calculateAllocatedAmount and revert distribution (repeat of prior audit L-01, re-confirmed by execution).
evidence: Executed: single-recipient split with allocation = totalAllocation = type(uint256).max and 3 ether funded reverts on distribute (test_ExtremeAllocationsRevert passes).
runtimeTrigger: Create split with max allocations; distribute reverts; funds locked until owner updates the split.

claim: AutoEarnEnrollerModule.enroll trusts any contract's owner() claim, so a non-SmartVault contract reporting the treasury as owner can get the earn module 'enabled' on it and emit a misleading Enrolled event.
evidence: enroll only checks code existence and account_.owner() == treasury; no check that account_ is a genuine SmartVault.
runtimeTrigger: Deploy a contract whose owner() returns a treasury; call enroll; Enrolled event emitted for a non-vault.

claim: WebAuthn.verify does not check the origin or rpIdHash, so a passkey assertion minted for another relying party could be replayed if the challenge collides.
evidence: The verify docstring lists origin and rpIdHash checks as explicitly NOT performed; only challenge, type, UP bit and the P-256 signature are verified.
runtimeTrigger: Victim completes a WebAuthn ceremony on a malicious RP for the same challenge bytes; attacker replays the assertion.

claim: SplitsWarehouse._withdraw sends ETH with full gas (sendValue) after burning, so a reentrant owner/withdrawer could multiply withdrawals or incentive rewards.
evidence: _withdraw burns then calls payable.sendValue (full gas) to owner and withdrawer; reentrancy into withdraw() is possible mid-payout.
runtimeTrigger: Malicious withdrawer reenters batch withdraw from receive() to claim the incentive repeatedly.
